migration.rule: Internal history records are not bundled into customer snapshots.

modes.label: User View
modes.intent: Installed customer workbench for running, editing, creating, and improving agents.
securityNotes: Platform source tree is excluded from the customer bundle snapshot.

productPosition.productClaim: A desktop platform whose core is Agent Core for easy custom agent and subagent creation plus CLI orchestration for continuous Codex, Claude Code, Gemini, OpenCode, and other guest CLI work with deferred decisions and task-run records. Root tools, workspace workbench, learning, and observability support those two core capabilities.

desktopHomeSurface.homeCopyRule: The first screen shall emphasize Agent Core, CLI orchestration continuity, Tool Studio for shared root tools, EVAL for current work quality, and at-a-glance work visibility before deeper observability details.
desktopHomeSurface.configurationRule: Core setup for provider accounts, CLI adapters, root tools, workspace access, and question deferral shall be visible from Home and collected in the execution settings surface.

featureLayers.label: CLI Orchestration
featureLayers.purpose: Coordinate local/provider model tasks and optional CLI lanes as a supervised task graph with bounded IO, decision routing, merge gates, and cleanup.
featureLayers.userOutcome: The user starts one task from chat and the platform runs the selected local/provider model or specialized lanes, pauses only dependent decisions, and keeps independent work moving.
automationTargets: direct model task execution from local Ollama models or connected OpenAI, Anthropic, or Gemini accounts
native local model catalog refresh through list_provider_models
provider credential injection into guest CLI sessions
top-level run configuration selection for search agent, CLI session, task pipe, and workspace readiness
Services-style inspection of runtime, workspace, adapters, providers, and active sessions
Problems-style surfacing of missing runtime, missing adapters, missing model accounts, pending decisions, dirty drafts, and release blockers
AgentCore-style blueprint to native agent proposal creation
local Python agent execution with remote services treated as tool connectors
production agent blueprint selection for runtime, memory, gateway, and evaluation patterns

featureLayers.label: Agent Work Environment
featureLayers.purpose: Host app-selected workspaces, runtime data stores, task-run records, decisions, support diagnostics, and agent work planes.
featureLayers.userOutcome: The user no longer has to manually clone and work from a terminal-first folder; the app owns workspace selection and accumulated data access.

featureLayers.label: Agent Development Environment
featureLayers.purpose: Provide the developer workbench for source review, multi-file edits, diffs, templates, requirements, specs, validation, and runtime contracts.
featureLayers.userOutcome: The user can shape agent platform behavior inside a desktop workbench instead of bouncing between loose files and terminal-only flows.

featureLayers.label: Agent Core
featureLayers.purpose: Turn repeated work into prompts, workflows, templates, tools, skills, agents, and finally platform features with traceable decisions.
featureLayers.userOutcome: The user can create agents and reusable capabilities without repeatedly telling the assistant the same process.
learningSignals: agent proposal saved from AgentCore-style blueprint

featureLayers.label: Learning & Evaluation Loop
featureLayers.purpose: Accumulate work history, timing, evaluations, web searches, intent maps, evidence, and improvement records so platform behavior gets better over time.
featureLayers.userOutcome: The user can see why the platform improved, what evidence drove changes, and which gaps remain.

featureLayers.label: Root Tool Management
featureLayers.purpose: Keep shared provider accounts, CLI adapters, workspace files, source tools, and decision-routing defaults outside individual tasks so every custom agent and guest CLI lane can reuse the same root tool base.
featureLayers.userOutcome: The user configures root tools once, then task-specific agents, subagents, and CLI lanes can share them without duplicated setup.
automationTargets: root tool sharing across task-specific agents

featureLayers.label: Work Visibility
featureLayers.purpose: Show the amount of active work, deferred decisions, task-run records, and available agents at a glance so work is not forgotten while long-running agent or CLI tasks continue.
featureLayers.userOutcome: The user can immediately see what is running, what is blocked, what was recorded, and where to resume.

featureLayers.label: Observability & Monitoring
featureLayers.purpose: Expose structure, history, documents, source inventory, diagnostics, and status so the primary agent platform features can be understood and trusted.
featureLayers.userOutcome: The user can inspect accumulated data and platform state without mistaking that inspection layer for the whole product.

promotionLoop.improvementRule: When repeated human work, agent failures, omitted steps, validation failures, or useful patterns recur, create the smallest durable asset first and promote only when evidence justifies a larger feature.

qualitySignals: The first screen names Agent Core and CLI orchestration before root tools, workbench, learning, or observability.
Tool Studio gives root tools, Python runtime setup, and deployment their own work-first surface separate from task-specific agent creation and CLI orchestration surfaces.
Current work volume, deferred decisions, task-run records, and agent count are visible at a glance.
Snapshot data includes product feature architecture for developer and customer builds.
Customer snapshot preserves sellable feature structure but removes internal source paths and validation internals.
Readiness tests fail if monitoring is positioned as the primary product.
New feature work updates requirements, specs, validation, history, and request traces.
AgentCore-style blueprint choices map reference samples to runnable local product flows.
Desktop Runtime starts from run configurations and tool-window status instead of making the user scan a web dashboard.
Resident desktop/source panels share native warmup and source-catalog prepare requests instead of duplicating OS work.
AWS deployment remains optional; the installed desktop app owns task state and accumulated records.

productPosition.purpose: 레퍼런스 앱의 장점을 복사하는 것이 아니라, 에이전트 플랫폼의 핵심 작업 루프에 맞춰 재구성한다.
productPosition.primaryRule: 작업 시작, 에이전트 오케스트레이션, 파일/코드 조작, 검증, 학습 개선이 첫 화면의 중심이어야 한다.
productPosition.customerPromise: 사용자는 앱을 켜고 워크스페이스를 선택한 뒤 파일, 터미널, 에이전트, 검증, 히스토리를 한 데스크톱 워크벤치에서 다룬다.
productPosition.monitoringBoundary: 모니터링과 운영자 기능은 상태 확인, 감사, 복구를 돕는 보조면으로 분리한다.

platformGroups.strongestAdvantage: activity rail, side bar, editor center, tool windows, bottom terminal/output panel, status bar
platformGroups.transferRule: 우리 앱은 웹 대시보드가 아니라 단일 네이티브 워크벤치여야 하며, 중복 사이드바를 제거하고 아래 패널을 터미널/로그/검증에 배정한다.

platformGroups.strongestAdvantage: chat/thread workbench, agent sidepane, diff review, background agents, rules, memories, workflows, skills, MCP connectors, checkpoints
platformGroups.transferRule: 에이전트가 어디서 일하는지, 어떤 권한과 규칙으로 움직이는지, 어떤 로컬 도구와 연결됐는지, 변경을 어떻게 되돌리는지를 항상 사용자가 볼 수 있어야 한다.

platformGroups.strongestAdvantage: tool approval, CLI/scriptability, SDKs, PR checks, slash-command orchestration, skills/MCP surfaces, embedded editor/terminal/browser lanes
platformGroups.transferRule: 성숙한 오픈소스 기능은 게스트 어댑터 또는 엔진 후보로 평가하되, 플랫폼의 데이터/권한/검증 경계가 우선한다.

platformGroups.strongestAdvantage: one-click setup, settings dialogs, troubleshooting, command palette, channels/spaces, visual confirmation
platformGroups.transferRule: 설정과 복구는 팝업/전용 패널에 두고, 반복 작업은 커맨드 팔레트와 확장 카탈로그로 빠르게 실행한다.

transferPatterns.labelKo: 단일 사이드바 + 중앙 작업대 + 하단 터미널
transferPatterns.labelEn: Single activity rail, workbench center, bottom terminal
transferPatterns.observedStrength: Mature desktop apps separate navigation, editor/work area, terminal/output, and status so users do not scroll through one long web page.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Keep one primary sidebar, route feature tabs into the workbench center, and reserve the bottom drawer for multi-CLI terminal, logs, validation, and task runs.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자가 어디서 파일을 보고, 어디서 명령을 실행하고, 어디서 결과를 확인하는지 즉시 이해한다.
implementationTargets: keep CLI drawer as bottom/full overlay
use drill-down child views instead of combining multiple functions in one tab

transferPatterns.labelEn: Run Configurations, Services, and Problems workbench
transferPatterns.observedStrength: IntelliJ puts runnable configurations, tool windows, service state, and problem inspection close to the work surface so the user can start, inspect, and fix work without hunting through a dashboard.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Desktop Runtime starts with an IDE-style Run Configuration toolbar and connected Services, Problems, and status-bar regions for search agent, CLI session, task pipe, workspace readiness, providers, adapters, sessions, decisions, and blockers.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 검색 에이전트 실행, CLI 세션, 다중 파이프, 준비 점검을 한 화면의 IDE식 실행 영역에서 바로 시작하고 막힌 이유를 즉시 본다.
implementationTargets: Run Configuration cards call real search agent, CLI session, task pipe, and readiness actions
Services list shows runtime, workspace, adapters, providers, and active sessions
Problems strip links blockers to terminal, settings, questions, or readiness checks
status bar summarizes runtime, CLI, model, sessions, inbox, and terminal state
riskControls: readiness script requires the new workbench tokens
responsive CSS keeps the tool-window layout usable on smaller screens

transferPatterns.observedStrength: The Codex app treats each task as a desktop thread with project scope, command menu, slash commands, terminal, Git/diff, worktree mode, artifacts, skills, MCP, browser, and approval controls around one work unit.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Treat each agent run chat as a first-class workbench thread: the composer starts work, the bottom panel owns terminal output, the side/inspector area shows files, diff, artifacts, decisions, validations, and a mode selector keeps Local/Worktree/Cloud-like execution explicit.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 검색 에이전트나 다른 에이전트를 실행할 때 채팅, 파일, 터미널, 변경사항, 검증, 기록이 같은 작업 단위로 묶인다는 것을 바로 이해한다.
implementationTargets: every runnable agent opens as a work chat thread
slash-command suggestions in the work chat composer for status, plan, review, terminal, files, and skills
mode selector for direct workspace, isolated worktree, and future remote execution
riskControls: approval and sandbox scope visible before privileged actions

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Claude Desktop makes local MCP capabilities easier to use by managing desktop extensions in settings, surfacing connector status from the chat composer, and making installed tools available in conversations.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Put local tools, MCP servers, and CLI adapters behind one Settings > Capabilities surface, then expose connected capability chips and tool status directly in agent work chats instead of making users edit JSON or type shell bootstrap commands.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 설정에서 로컬 도구를 연결하고, 채팅창에서 어떤 도구가 붙어 있는지 확인한 뒤 바로 작업을 시작한다.
implementationTargets: Settings > Capabilities tab for MCP servers, desktop extensions, and guest CLI adapters
connector chips beside every agent chat composer
one-click install or setup guide for optional local tools
debug log and missing-capability recovery panel
riskControls: sensitive fields use OS secure storage or redacted secret references
enterprise allowlist and disabled connector states are explicit

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Useful agent products frame work as async tasks with status, follow-up, takeover, validation, branch/workspace isolation, and review.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Represent every launched agent task as a platform-owned run record with workspace, lane, command, output, evidence, validation, handoff, and review status.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 터미널을 직접 붙잡고 있지 않아도 작업 상태와 결과를 앱에서 이어받는다.
riskControls: tool permission prompts for destructive commands

transferPatterns.labelEn: Rules, memory, workflows, and skills are separate
transferPatterns.observedStrength: Users understand configuration better when durable rules, auto memory, manual workflows, reusable skills, and agent definitions are not mixed together.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: The Settings and Agent Core surfaces must make this taxonomy explicit and save each asset into the correct durable path.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 뭘 설정해야 하는지 몰라 헤매지 않고, 반복 작업을 올바른 자산으로 승격한다.
implementationTargets: one settings button with tabs for provider, workspace, rules, memory, workflows, skills, permissions
agent init wizard writes AGENTS.md/rules/skills with preview
riskControls: never write private memories into versioned rules without explicit approval
show activation mode and scope before saving

transferPatterns.observedStrength: The public Claw Code docs frame agent work around slash commands, team-style parallel review, persistent execution loops, skills discovery, config inspection, and CLI bootstrap/init flows.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Expose agent commands, task pipe presets, team/review lanes, skills, and init/doctor/status actions as platform-managed command palette entries instead of hiding them in ad hoc terminal prompts.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 터미널 명령을 외우지 않고, 에이전트 팀 실행과 검증 루프를 앱의 명령/프리셋으로 시작한다.
implementationTargets: command palette entries for init, status, doctor, skills, and team review
task pipe lane for orchestration critique
setup guidance when claw is missing

transferPatterns.observedStrength: The Claw Code public docs keep implementation surfaces, command/tool inventories, verification commands, and parity gaps explicit so incomplete ports do not look complete.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Keep every adapter, runtime surface, source editor capability, and generated command family tied to a manifest, parity gap, readiness test, and user-visible capability state.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 실제 구현된 것과 아직 계약/대기 상태인 것을 구분하고, 불완전한 기능을 완성품으로 오해하지 않는다.
implementationTargets: capability parity matrix for each CLI adapter
adapter command inventory in accumulated data
readiness guard for supported adapter list
customer-visible status labels for implemented versus integrated_contract
riskControls: do not mark source-unverified references as copied implementation

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Agent tools are safer and easier to trust when pre-tool checks, permission requests, action approval, post-tool logging, and rollback points are visible.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Add a platform permission layer before guest CLI actions and store approval, denial, checkpoint, and rollback records in the runtime data plane.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 파일 수정, 명령 실행, 브라우저 사용, 외부 도구 호출이 앱 안에서 승인되고 되돌릴 수 있다.

transferPatterns.labelKo: 파일 탐색과 코드 편집/디프 리뷰 내장
transferPatterns.labelEn: Embedded file explorer, editor, and diff review
transferPatterns.observedStrength: Developer desktop tools make the file system and proposed changes visible before commit or handoff.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Use the native file workspace and Monaco/source review panes as first-class product surfaces, not a hidden monitoring detail.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 파일시스템을 끌어와 코드와 설정을 직접 보고, 에이전트가 바꾼 내용을 검토한다.
riskControls: customer snapshot strips source file content

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Specialized agents work better when they have narrow prompts, scoped tools, separate context, and clear delegation rules.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Agent Core creates named agents, subagents, skills, tools, prompts, validation gates, and promotion records from repeated human work.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 같은 지시를 반복하지 않고 목적별 에이전트를 쉽게 만들고 개선한다.

transferPatterns.observedStrength: AI coding products gain trust when checks are explicit, repeatable, visible in PR/task lifecycle, and actionable when they fail.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Represent lint, test, config contract, release readiness, customer bundle audit, and hallucination/security checks as run gates with evidence.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 에이전트가 만든 결과가 왜 통과했는지, 어디서 실패했는지, 다음 개선점이 뭔지 본다.
riskControls: no unsupported factual claim without source
record command, exit code, and evidence target

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Good desktop products own install, settings, diagnostics, update, data location, and local runtime boundaries instead of making users run many commands.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: The platform launches first, owns runtime data and UI authority, and invokes guest CLIs or sidecars through explicit adapters.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 명령어를 하나씩 몰라도 앱 설치, 데이터 경로, 진단, 업데이트, 실행을 한 곳에서 관리한다.

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Fast launcher apps reduce friction by making commands searchable, installable, and keyboard-first.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Expose actions such as open workspace, start agent, init rules, run validation, install adapter, and show diagnostics through a desktop command palette.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 메뉴를 찾아다니지 않고 지금 필요한 기능을 검색해서 실행한다.
riskControls: missing adapters show setup guidance instead of blocking the app

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Channel-like organization and decision queues help users separate projects, tasks, handoffs, approvals, and notifications.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Use projects/spaces for work boundaries and a decision inbox for blocked agent questions, permission requests, merge gates, and follow-ups.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 여러 에이전트 작업을 채널처럼 분리하고, 답해야 할 것만 한 곳에서 처리한다.
riskControls: client-side hiding is not treated as security

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Tool ecosystems become safer when scopes, consent, auth, server trust, tool search, and elicitation are visible.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: The platform must manage MCP servers and CLI adapters as capability records with trust level, scope, auth status, and permission prompts.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 에이전트가 어떤 외부 도구와 데이터에 접근하는지 보고 제어한다.

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Agentic systems need design-time controls for indirect prompt injection, excessive agency, external content, secrets, and high-risk tools.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Treat untrusted files/web/docs/logs as data, keep least privilege defaults, require human approval for high-risk actions, and record every exception.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 자동화가 편해져도 권한, 외부 입력, 비밀, 위험 명령이 무방비로 실행되지 않는다고 판단할 수 있다.

transferPatterns.labelKo: 사용/평가 데이터 기반 학습 개선 루프
transferPatterns.labelEn: Learning loop from usage and evaluation data
transferPatterns.observedStrength: Users trust agent platforms more when performance, outcomes, memories, decisions, and repeated failures are inspectable and improve future runs.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Persist task runs, decisions, evidence, work timing, evaluations, intent maps, and promotion candidates so the platform can improve agents and capabilities over time.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 플랫폼은 작업을 쌓아두기만 하지 않고 반복 병목과 성공 패턴을 기능/에이전트 개선으로 되돌린다.
riskControls: private data stays out of shared memory
AWS AgentCore CLI and credentials remain optional deployment adapters
Lambda or other cloud functions may be remote tool connectors but are not the agent execution host

patterns.label: Web-first research
patterns.purpose: Confirm unstable or tool-specific facts with current primary sources before planning, editing, or claiming readiness.
triggerWhen: The user asks for latest, current, best practice, open-source references, packaging, API behavior, or broad platform design.
A task depends on a page, repository, library, or documentation not already loaded into context.
sequence: Search high-authority sources first.
Prefer official docs for implementation behavior.
Record queries, checked sources, weak sources ignored, plan impact, and uncertainty.
Only carry source claims into implementation when the source changes the plan or risk model.
failureModes: Using stale model memory for changed library behavior.
Treating community signals as factual proof.
Forgetting to carry source uncertainty into the plan.
patterns.platformApplication: Tool Studio should show research as a first gate for tool creation, validation, packaging, and external integration work.

patterns.label: Parallel local inspection
patterns.purpose: Read existing source, tests, configs, and docs quickly without flooding the operator with noisy shell output.
triggerWhen: The task needs repo context across source, UI, tests, configs, and docs.
Multiple read-only inspections can run without touching shared mutable state.
sequence: Start with git status and targeted file maps.
Use rg for text and file discovery.
Read related source files in parallel when they are independent.
Summarize the system shape before editing.
failureModes: Reading too much source by default.
Running parallel commands that mutate the same file or git state.
Chaining shell output into unreadable logs.
patterns.platformApplication: A future desktop source-intake lane can precompute read-only maps and expose them beside the code editor.

patterns.label: Snapshot worker thread pool
patterns.purpose: Use multiple Node worker threads for independent document rendering and source preview work during startup snapshot collection.
triggerWhen: The monitor must transform hundreds or thousands of independent documents.
Source previews can be read independently and sorted after processing.
Startup snapshot collection becomes a visible boot-time cost.
sequence: Collect document and source-file tasks without reading every payload.
Choose worker count from available CPU parallelism and task count.
Run document rendering and source preview extraction through a bounded worker pool.
Fall back to the previous synchronous path if worker startup or execution fails.
Record worker counts in the generated snapshot stats.
evidenceOutputs: collect timing with CPU utilization above one core
failureModes: Spawning too many workers and making small repositories slower.
Assuming worker parallelism helps network or UI-bound work.
Dropping deterministic sorting after parallel task completion.
patterns.platformApplication: Workspace Monitor startup collection now uses CPU-aware worker parallelism while preserving deterministic snapshots and synchronous fallback.

patterns.label: Patch-based editing
patterns.purpose: Make scoped source changes with reviewable diffs while preserving user work and avoiding destructive operations.
triggerWhen: A source, config, test, or document change is needed.
The worktree may include user changes that must not be reverted.
sequence: Announce the edit target and intent.
Apply the smallest coherent patch.
Inspect the diff after edits.
Avoid reset, checkout, or deletion unless the user explicitly requested it.
failureModes: Overwriting unrelated user edits.
Refactoring beyond the requested behavioral surface.
Editing generated files before the source of truth.
patterns.platformApplication: Source workbench should support patch queues, diff preview, and protected user-change boundaries.

patterns.label: Renderer validation loop
patterns.purpose: Validate TypeScript, collector contracts, static UI rules, browser rendering, and performance-sensitive surfaces before packaging.
triggerWhen: Workspace Monitor source, snapshot schema, UI, CSS, or generated data changes.
A user-reported interaction or rendering problem is being fixed.
sequence: Regenerate the workspace snapshot.
Run TypeScript and source contract checks.
Run node --test suites.
Open the relevant UI route with a browser smoke check.
Check visible text, stable controls, and nonblank surfaces.
failureModes: Passing static tests while the UI route is blank.
Updating UI without the snapshot schema.
Forgetting to regenerate developer snapshot after customer packaging.
patterns.platformApplication: Tool Studio should expose the renderer validation ladder directly beside build and deployment controls.

patterns.label: Desktop packaging loop
patterns.purpose: Turn a verified renderer and Tauri shell into local macOS artifacts without making the user run build steps manually.
triggerWhen: The user asks for runnable desktop app changes.
Renderer, Tauri command, native process, packaging, or installer-adjacent behavior changes.
sequence: Prepare the renderer snapshot and static output.
Run the internal desktop packaging command.
Verify .app and DMG artifact paths.
Record public-readiness gaps separately from local internal readiness.
failureModes: Claiming public macOS readiness without notarization and hardened-runtime gates.
Leaving customer snapshot in place after internal packaging.
Treating a web build as enough for desktop runtime changes.
patterns.platformApplication: Desktop Runtime and Tool Studio should show packaging as a first-class validation ladder, not an afterthought.

patterns.label: Resource cleanup loop
patterns.purpose: Prevent leaking dev servers, browser sessions, PTYs, subprocess pipes, timers, caches, or native runtime handles.
triggerWhen: The task starts a server, browser automation, terminal session, subprocess, worker, queue, stream, timer, or native resource.
A desktop optimization touches CPU, RAM, PTY, pipes, or cache behavior.
sequence: Name every long-running resource before starting it.
Attach a stop, close, or dispose action.
Confirm cleanup before final response.
Record residual resource risk when cleanup cannot be proven.
failureModes: Leaving dev servers running after verification.
Keeping stale browser tabs or PTY sessions alive.
Holding file handles or pipes across task boundaries.
patterns.platformApplication: Native runtime panels should expose process and pipe lifecycle state as part of task health.

patterns.label: Git close-out loop
patterns.purpose: Turn a completed change set into an auditable commit and push only after validation and final evaluation records exist.
triggerWhen: A meaningful source, config, documentation, or history change is complete.
Repository rules require commit and push for completed work.
sequence: Review the diff and changed paths.
Run required validation and package steps.
Write work summary, evaluation, omission check, and trace records.
Commit with a scoped conventional message.
Push to origin/main unless explicitly told not to.
failureModes: Committing before validation artifacts exist.
Bundling unrelated user changes.
Leaving the user to run the final build.
patterns.platformApplication: The platform should make finalization explicit: evidence, validation, commit, push, and artifact paths.

verificationLadders.label: Workspace Monitor source ladder
acceptance: Tool Studio renders the Agent Tool Playbook.
Static tests cover collector, UI, and snapshot type contracts.

verificationLadders.label: Parallel snapshot ladder
acceptance: snapshotDocumentWorkers is greater than one on multi-core developer machines with enough documents.
snapshotSourceWorkers is greater than one when enough source candidates exist.
Generated documents and source files remain deterministic after parallel processing.

verificationLadders.label: Desktop package ladder
acceptance: Internal .app and DMG artifacts are generated.
Public-readiness caveats remain separate from internal runnable artifacts.
Developer snapshot is restored after customer bundle generation when needed.

verificationLadders.label: Runtime resource ladder
acceptance: Dev servers and browser sessions started by the task are stopped.
Long-running processes are named and have cleanup actions.
Residual risk is recorded when cleanup cannot be proven.

adoptionBacklog.title: Turn playbook entries into executable task presets
riskControls: Install and external mutation steps require explicit approval.
Every preset records evidence and rollback.

adoptionBacklog.title: Persist tool-call traces and validation ladders per task run
riskControls: Keep raw logs separate from operator summaries.

checklist: sourceFiles are removed from the installer bundle snapshot.
Internal documents, history, specs, and requirements are removed from the installer bundle snapshot.
Runtime data is loaded through Tauri commands after the installed app starts.
